Of the 3 routes proposed in 2019 (Routes 5a, 5b and 5c), Route 5b has definitively taken precedence. I've changed the spreadsheet listing and wiki page name from Route 5b to Route 5. Routes 5a and 5c have been marked as "Cancelled" as of July 2024, given the lack of news about the latter two options since November 2019.

column109: CB: route from gulfpub — GulfPub 'Badr el Din 2 - Badr el Din' trace (26.8 km) matches the BED-2->BED-3 corridor the research corroborated. BAPETCO's BED concession (Abu Gharadig basin, ~300 km west of Cairo per nsenergybusiness.com) contains numbered sub-fields BED-1/BED-2/BED-3, developed together as one cluster. Farmout Angel's coordinates for BED-2 and BED-3 are mutually consistent (~25 km apart) and closely match GulfPub's cited 26.8 km 'Badr el Din 2 - Badr el Din' trace -- the strongest evidence found for what this 'Spur (1)' pipeline actually connects. Deliberately did NOT use the payload's facility_anchor coordinate for 'Bed-2 Oil and Gas Field (Matrouh, Egypt)' (lon=26.66, lat=30.26): it sits ~190 km WNW of the BED-1/BED-3 cluster, geographically implausible for a field developed as part of the same concession as BED-3 -- flagging this as a likely mismapped coordinate in the internal GOGET dataset, not a basis for a route. Single-source coordinates (Farmout Angel) for both endpoints; a second independent geocoding source would strengthen this further, but the distance/order-of-magnitude match to GulfPub's trace gives reasonable confidence. No dedicated Arabic-language article found describing this specific spur by name. SHEET CONFLICT: Sheet gives 130.0 km for this spur; independent coordinates for BED-2 and BED-3 put a two-point great-circle distance at ~25 km, which sits inside the disputed-range window the prior researcher flagged (GulfPub reports comparable BED lines at 19-63 km, with a specific 'Badr el Din 2 - Badr el Din Pipeline' trace of 26.8 km matching this corridor closely). The sheet's 130 km figure looks materially overstated for this corridor. Suggest StartLocation -> 'Badr El Din 2 (BED-2) Field'. Suggest EndLocation -> 'Badr El Din 3 (BED-3) gas processing facility'.

column109: CB: route from gulfpub — GulfPub 'Badr el Din Field - Alam El Shawish' trace (70 km) matches the BED-3->Alam El Shawish corridor the research corroborated. Two-point candidate uses BED-3 (documented tie-in hub) and the Alam El Shawish West concession centroid; straight-line distance is only ~16 km, well under both GulfPub's 70 km trace and the ~47 km summed pipeline-segment figure from Egypt Oil & Gas -- expected, since concession-block centroids don't reflect actual routing across a ~1,075 km2 block to specific well clusters (Assil/Karam sit within, not necessarily at, the block centroid). A separate Egypt Oil & Gas piece ('Field Development back on track') independently confirms Alam El Shawish and Badr El-Din are linked by transport infrastructure (for crude oil rather than this gas spur), corroborating the two fields as pipeline-connected neighbors. On the P3937/P3938 duplicate question: found evidence these are TWO DISTINCT real corridors radiating from the BED-3 hub in different directions (P3937 west/short to BED-2, P3938 west-southwest to Alam El Shawish/Assil-Karam) -- not duplicates of each other -- but the sheet's shared, unverified 130 km length for both looks like a data error that should be corrected downward for both rows rather than treated as ground truth. Confidence: moderate -- endpoint identification and general corridor direction are reasonably corroborated by 2+ independent sources (Farmout Angel coordinates + Egypt Oil & Gas pipeline description), but exact routing/length remains uncertain. SHEET CONFLICT: Sheet gives 130.0 km, identical to P3937's figure for a completely different corridor -- the two rows sharing the exact same length looks like a duplication/copy error rather than two independently measured pipelines. Egypt Oil & Gas ('Assil and Karam fields on the development track') documents real gathering pipelines from the Alam El Shawish West concession's Assil/Karam gas development tying into BED-3: a 24 km 12-in line, a 12 km 12-in line, and an 11.3 km 8-in line (~47 km summed across segments) -- same order of magnitude as GulfPub's cited 70 km 'Badr el Din Field - Alam El Shawish' trace, and far short of the sheet's 130 km. Likely origin of the '130' figure: an unrelated Oil & Gas Journal CO2-EOR study describes gathering CO2-rich gas from four DIFFERENT Western Desert plants (Obaiyed, El Salam, Tarek, El Qasr) to a central point in El Salam, then piping it 130 MILES (not km) to Abu Sennan field for storage -- a different corridor entirely (El Salam-to-Abu Sennan, not BED-to-Alam El Shawish) and a proposed/study concept, not confirmed built infrastructure. Plausible the sheet's '130' for both BED spurs is a garbled echo of this unrelated 130-mile CO2 study number rather than a real measurement of either spur. Suggest StartLocation -> 'Badr El Din 3 (BED-3) gas processing facility'. Suggest EndLocation -> 'Alam El Shawish West field/concession'.

column109: CB: route guessed from endpoints — Runs generally north-to-south down the Baghdad governorate: from Taji (~25-30 km north of central Baghdad) to the Al-Dora/Daura district on the south side of the city (Dora oil refinery and Al-Dora thermal/gas power stations). Straight-line ~28 km; a routed alignment skirting/through the metro is plausibly ~45-55 km, consistent with the likely-duplicate P1845 'Taji-South Baghdad' length of 56 km. Endpoints are named at town/facility scale and independently verifiable; the intermediate alignment is NOT sourced -- treat as a loose Baghdad-governorate corridor, not a traced route. Endpoints established from the pipeline NAME (Taji -> Duara/Dora) plus the Jafar/Uruk map placing the line on the north-south Baghdad dry-gas backbone. The two proposed_refs are verifier-passing and confirm the ENDPOINTS exist as real Baghdad-area places (Taji town north of Baghdad; Al-Dora power station in Dora, south Baghdad) -- they do NOT independently confirm the pipeline between them. Coordinates are approximate, decimal-degree EPSG:4326, defensible from these named, well-known places (Taji town center ~33.52N 44.23E; Dora refinery/power complex, south Baghdad ~33.27N 44.40E); no coordinate was fabricated and the intermediate waypoint is an approximate metro transit point, not a sourced vertex. If the row is merged into P1845 per the duplicate finding, transfer this corridor there.

column109: CB: route guessed from endpoints — This GEM row/segment is confirmed to be specifically the 独山-平塘段 (Dushan-Pingtang section) of the larger 独山-平塘-罗甸天然气支线管道工程 (Dushan-Pingtang-Luodian branch pipeline project) — sources explicitly parenthesize '(独山-平塘段)' when naming the project, and describe it as ending at the boundary of/entering Pingtang County, i.e. it does NOT extend to Luodian. Gas source: the branch connects to the Sino-Myanmar (China-Myanmar) gas pipeline within Dushan County via a separate feeder (see duplicate-check note below), then runs from a Dushan-side gate/distribution station near Yangfeng (former Yangfeng Township, absorbed into Baiquan Town in a July 2013 administrative merger along with Chengguan Town and Yaosuo Township — per Baidu Baike '羊凤乡' entry) across the county line into Pingtang County. The Dushan gov site (dushan.gov.cn) explicitly groups three components of Dushan's natural-gas 'county-to-county' (县县通) build-out: (1) 贵州天然气管网独山天然气支线 (the Dushan branch, = GEM P4954, 11.55km, Dagang Village to Dushan), (2) 独山-平塘-罗甸天然气支线项目(独山-平塘段) (this row, P4955, 15.20km per GEM / reported as ~17.3km new pipe in one secondary source — the discrepancy is unresolved but both describe the same Dushan-Pingtang leg), and (3) 天然气门站 (a gate station) — identified by name as 羊凤天然气门站, which completed acceptance/registration Aug 2023 and reportedly began commissioning June 2023. Design specs from search snippets (not independently re-verified against a primary PDF): L360N steel pipe, DN323.9mm, 6.3 MPa design pressure, ~1.5 × 10^8 m³/year design capacity, ~120 million yuan investment, National Pipeline Group Southwest Pipeline Co. (国家管网集团西南管道公司) as builder. Straight-line distance between the geocoded start (Yangfeng) and end (Pingtang county seat) points is ~15km, consistent with the sheet's 15.20km LengthMergedKm and giving reasonable confidence the two points bracket the real corridor, though the pipeline's actual routing along roads/terrain will differ from a straight line and the true terminus may be short of the county seat itself. | P4955 is NOT a duplicate of P4954 (Dagang Village–Dushan County, 11.55km, operating) — that row is the separate 独山天然气支线 (Dushan branch) that feeds gas IN to Dushan from the 47# valve chamber on the Sino-Myanmar pipeline; P4955 is the onward Dushan-Pingtang leg. Checked the GGIT snapshot for other Guizhou rows mentioning Pingtang/Luodian/Dushan: P4989 ('Sino-Myanmar Fuquan Branch Pipeline 47# Valve Chamber' to 'Luodian', 110km, construction) and P4991 (Wangmo to Luodian, 80km, proposed) both reach Luodian but via routes that do NOT mention Pingtang and start from a different valve chamber — these look like a separate corridor into Luodian, not a continuation of this Dushan-Pingtang segment, so no duplicate flag was set for those either, but a human reviewer assembling the full 独山-平塘-罗甸 corridor may want to check whether P4989's routing actually passes through/near Pingtang. (贵州昆仑天然气有限公司/毕节昆仑天然气有限公司), approved Feb 2015, construction started Aug 2015. Confirmed route order (both nyj.guizhou.gov.cn-sourced prose and the thepaper.cn acceptance article) runs 播州区 (Bozhou District, Zunyi) → 金沙县 (Jinsha County) → 大方县 (Dafang County) → 七星关区 (Qixingguan District, the seat of Bijie City) → 赫章县 (Hezhang County). P4957's own name/notes restrict its scope to the Zunyi-to-Qixingguan (i.e. Zunyi-to-Bijie) portion of that corridor, not the full line to Hezhang. First phase (遵义南输气站 [Zunyi South Gas Transmission Station] to 大方6号阀室 [Dafang No.6 valve room], 137km) went into trial operation/production at a June 4, 2018 ceremony at the Jinsha Clean Gas Distribution Station in Anlo Township, Jinsha County; the full 310.6km line passed formal completion acceptance May 17-18, 2022, with the inspection team visiting three checkpoints along the route: 播州区2号阀室 (Bozhou District No.2 valve room, near the Zunyi/start end), 七星关区清管分输站 (Qixingguan District pigging/distribution station), and a Hezhang geological-hazard point (赫章HZ002号桩地灾点, near the far end, outside P4957's scope). Within Qixingguan District specifically, a 2024 land-acquisition notice confirms the pipeline right-of-way crosses four townships in this order as listed: 岔河镇亦乐村 (Yile Village, Chahe Township), 阴底彝族苗族白族乡路朗村 (Lulang Village, Yindi Yi-Miao-Bai Autonomous Township), 杨家湾镇发达村 (Fada Village, Yangjiawan Township), and 朱昌镇八亩村 (Bamu Village, Zhuchang Township) — but the notice does not state which of these hosts 七星关区清管分输站, so the endpoint here is geocoded at the district level rather than to one specific township. | Likely overlap flag, not a confirmed duplicate: GEM already carries P6002 ('Guizhou Gas Pipeline Network' / SegmentName 'Zunyi-Hezhang Gas Pipeline', operating, StartProvince/EndProvince Guizhou/Guizhou), cited to https://www.bijie.gov.cn/bm/bjsnyj/dt/bmdt/202205/t20220519_74723533.html — a May 19, 2022 Bijie municipal government post whose dateline (one day after the May 17-18, 2022 completion-acceptance meeting I found independently via thepaper.cn) strongly suggests it is a local republish of the SAME completion-acceptance story, i.e. P6002 = the full 310.6km Zunyi-Hezhang trunk end-to-end. P4957's own pre-existing ResearcherNotes explicitly call it 'a segment of the Zunyi-Hezhang Gas Pipeline,' i.e. P4957 appears to be intended as a sub-segment (Zunyi-to-Qixingguan/Bijie portion only) carved out of the same physical line that P6002 represents at full length. Whether this is legitimate segment-vs-whole-line modeling (fine, if P6002 has no route of its own and is just a network-level rollup) or true geometry duplication (a problem, if P6002 is meant to carry its own full-length route) could not be determined from this task's scope — flagging P6002 for a human to check its own RouteAccuracy/geometry status before both rows are drawn. Both P4957's Qixingguan-side endpoint sourcing and P6002's own citation independently point to the same physical corridor, which is expected given the stated segment relationship, not treated as two independent corroborating sources for P4957's specific claims. The existing sheet reference for P4957 (https://archive.org/details/screenshot-2023-03-16-at-2.54.37-pm_202303, an archive.org screenshot page) was reviewed but not used: it is a generic Internet Archive item-detail page with no extractable pipeline-specific content, and independent primary/news sourcing (thepaper.cn completion-acceptance article, provincial 环保 EIA notice, Qixingguan district land-acquisition notices) was readily available and stronger. Two additional candidate sources that would have let me confirm '遵义南输气站' (Zunyi South Gas Transmission Station) by name as the literal origin station, and '大方6号阀室' as the first-phase terminus, could not be verified: 贵州省能源局/贵州省人民政府 (nyj.guizhou.gov.cn) 404'd with no Wayback snapshot available, and an in-en.com mirror of the same story 403'd. In their absence I used '播州区2号阀室,' independently confirmed via the verified thepaper.cn acceptance article, as the best-sourced named station near the start; this is corroborated at the district level by the Sept 2015 sthj.guizhou.gov.cn EIA notice, which locates the project in '遵义县' — the pre-Dec-2016 name for what is now 播州区 (Bozhou District).

On July 8, 2023, Xinjiang Autonomous Region government signed a strategic cooperation agreement with China National Petroleum Corporation (PetroChina). PetroChina will expand gas pipeline in Xinjiang with the mileage of 4977 kilometers. The expansion consists of 14 projects and will reach 10 municipalities in Xinjiang which have not been reached by gas pipeline. Among these pipeline projects, 5 will be deployed in Northern Xinjiang with 4.66 billion RMB budget, totalling 2863.5 kilometers. The other 9 projects will be deployed in Southern Xinjiang, totalling 2113.5 kilometers. The investment is expected to be 7.99 billion RMB.

The same news source also confirmed that the milage of Zungharia Basin Rim Gas Pipeline Network has reached 2067 kilometers, covering 9 municipalities and 7 million of population. The mileage of Tarim Basin Rim Gas Pipeline Network has reached 3037 kilometers, covering 4.3 million of population in 5 municipalities.

No details about these 14 projects are disclosed.

GEM's Wiki links this row to 'Zungharia Basin Rim Gas Pipeline Network' (准噶尔盆地周边天然气管网), consistent with what was found: a Karamay/Xinjiang-Oilfield hub (Jinlong Town + Karamay First Station, FuelSource = Karamay Oil Field) feeding gas 'benefit-the-people' (利民) branch pipelines that fan out to four northern prefectures — Tacheng, Altay, Ili (Yining), and Bortala (Bole) — plus a Karamay-to-Urumqi (Wangjiagou/Toutunhe) trunk, which matches GEM's existing StartLocation='Jinlong Town'/EndLocation='Wangjiagou' pair (both independently corroborated: Jinlong Town via a 2026 valve-well bidding notice at 'Jinlong Town First Station' in Karamay; Wangjiagou via CNPC Xinjiang Oilfield's registered 'Wangjiagou Oil & Gas Storage and Transport Center' in Urumqi's Toutunhe District). Altay and Bortala branches are each being built in two phases/segments (Kelamaili-Fuhai then Fuhai-Fuyun; Jinghe-Alashankou and Bole-Wenquan respectively), which is why their 'start'/'end' fields above span the full multi-phase corridor rather than a single short segment. Individual per-branch lengths as reported (Tacheng ~264-407 km depending on trunk-vs-trunk+branches count; Altay 246 km + 335.7 km; Bortala ~179-198 km combined) do not cleanly sum to the GEM total of 2863.5 km — this program is still under active construction/tendering as of mid-2026 and press figures for the same corridor vary by report date and by whether branch spurs are included. | Strong MULTI_BRANCH result: 5 distinct legs sourced, 4 of them (Tacheng, Altay, Ili, Bortala) from official Xinjiang prefecture/autonomous-region government (.gov.cn) sites or Xinhua/state media, plus the Karamay-Wangjiagou trunk independently corroborating GEM's own pre-existing StartLocation/EndLocation. Karamay-based sources consistently reference TWO similarly-spelled-in-pinyin-but-distinct places: 克拉玛依/Karamay (the city/oilfield) vs 克拉美丽/Kelamaili (a gas field further east/northeast, in Altay-prefecture territory near Fuhai) — do not conflate them when drawing candidate geometry.

It looks very likely that the 2023-announced '9 southern projects' were consolidated/rebranded into the 气化南疆 program by the time construction started in 2024, i.e. P6230 may be an earlier, less-developed snapshot of what P7448 now represents in more detail — but I could not find a document that explicitly equates the two, and a Kashgar-prefecture and Hotan-prefecture branch (found here) are not mentioned in any of the 气化南疆-specific sourcing for P7448, so P6230's scope may be somewhat broader than P7448's. column109: CB: route guessed from endpoints — Two levels of corroboration: (1) the pipeline's existence, name, 42in diameter and 20km length are confirmed by Ministry of Petroleum Decree 1883/2025 (gazetted 16 Dec 2025) via Giza Governorate's follow-on land-expropriation Decree 297/2026 (independently reported by dostor.org and vetogate.com, both quoting the same governorate decree text); (2) the corridor and purpose (expanding the national gas grid to underserved areas / boosting network pressure, built by Petrojet under GASCO, running through Giza and Monufia Governorates alongside the Regional Ring Road near Munshaat al-Qanater) are described in a third, independent article (agrinewz, reporting on a Giza Agriculture Directorate meeting about the project's land impact). Endpoint-precision caveat: the 'Solaimaneyah' start is the weaker of the two coordinates -- OSM has only one place of that name in Giza Governorate ('Hadaeq El-Solaimaneyah'), which is plausible but the great-circle distance to North Giza (~25.5km) runs longer than the pipeline's own stated 20km length, meaning this is very likely in the right area but not an exact tie-in point. A human GIS pass against the Regional Ring Road corridor would tighten this. SHEET CONFLICT: IMPORTANT: the prior facility_anchor supplied for this row's 'end' (GEM entity 'Giza Gas Field (Egypt)', lon 29.846/lat 31.703, marked non-citable) is a NAME-COLLISION MISMATCH and should not be used. That GEM entity is the offshore 'Giza' gas field, part of BP's West Nile Delta project ~65-85km off the Alexandria coast (per BP and offshore-technology.com reporting) -- it has nothing to do with 'North Giza' in this pipeline's name, which the sourced decree/press instead ties to an onshore corridor through Giza and Monufia Governorates near Munshaat al-Qanater (consistent with the North Giza power station's location). Sheet's plain 'Giza' as EndLocation is directionally fine but under-specific -- the official name is specifically 'North Giza' (شمال الجيزة), a defined area, not central Giza city. Start coord basis: OSM/Nominatim-geocoded village/district named 'Hadaeq El-Solaimaneyah' (postal code 12588), Giza Governorate -- the only place bearing the pipeline's own name ('Solaimaneyah') found in Giza Governorate via public gazetteer search. Flagged medium confidence: great-circle distance to the North Giza end (~25.5km) runs somewhat longer than the pipeline's stated 20km length, suggesting this may not be the exact tie-in point, only the nearest named match.. End coord basis: Wikidata Q56359846 (North Giza Power Station), a sourced coordinate for the power plant that anchors the 'North Giza' end of the corridor; the agrinewz article independently places the pipeline's path near Munshaat al-Qanater in the same area..

CB: route guessed from endpoints — Two independent Arabic-press reproductions (elwatannews, vetogate) of the same government decree text, plus a third (almasdar) that summarizes the decree's diameters/length/timeline -- all describe the identical cadastral route (36in tie-in at Beni Suef -> west along the Giza Canal/Beni Suef-Fayoum road -> ends in New Fayoum City), so this is well corroborated as an official, under-construction line, part of the 'Decent Life' (Hayah Karima) presidential initiative. Sheet length 18.5km vs. gazetted ~19km is a trivial rounding difference, not a conflict. Start-point coordinate is the weak link: the precise KM-0 tie-in site (near 'Ezbet Abdel Hafiz') has no independent public geocode, so Beni Suef city center is used as a loose stand-in -- flagged for a human GIS pass if precision matters. SHEET CONFLICT: Sheet has StartLocation='New Fayoum City' and EndLocation blank. Egyptian Ministry of Petroleum Decree 1884/2025 (gazetted 25 Dec 2025, Official Gazette issue 291-bis(b); reproduced verbatim by elwatannews and vetogate, corroborated by almasdar) describes this as the 'Beni Suef - New Fayoum' line: it STARTS at KM 0 on the existing Dahshur/Beni Suef 36in trunk line in Beni Suef Governorate and ENDS inside New Fayoum City at KM 19.000 (blow-off room 3). So the sheet has the correct place but on the wrong end -- New Fayoum City is the END, not the start, and the true start (Beni Suef) is missing from the sheet entirely. Start coord basis: Beni Suef city-center coordinate (Wikipedia infobox, 29°04'N 31°05'E) used as the nearest named/geocodable anchor. The gazetted route description places the actual tie-in (KM 0, blow-off room 1) several km west of the city in agricultural land near 'Ezbet Abdel Hafiz' -- that hamlet is not independently geocodable via OSM/Wikipedia, so the city center is a looser proxy; treat this endpoint's position as approximate.. End coord basis: New Faiyum, Wikipedia infobox coordinate (29°13'26"N 30°53'48"E) -- a real, established new urban community in Faiyum Governorate..

Developed via four subsea wells tied back across the Cyprus-Egypt EEZ boundary to existing Zohr field facilities (Shorouk Block, Egypt), then onward through Zohr's existing infrastructure to Damietta LNG for export as LNG to Europe. Both endpoints corroborated by multiple independent outlets (Offshore Magazine, Maritime Executive, ProtoThema, Drilling Contractor, Offshore Technology) reporting consistent distance figures, but the Cronos endpoint lacks a published survey coordinate, so its lon/lat here is a distance-triangulated approximation — good enough for an indicative corridor, not a precise route. All 7 route_refs re-verified via url_verifier.py (200 OK). SHEET CONFLICT: The sheet name 'Cronos-Port Said Gas Pipeline' is misleading and does not match what's actually being built. Per the FID announcement (28 July 2026, Eni/TotalEnergies), this is a trans-boundary subsea tieback connecting the Cronos wellhead directly to EXISTING ZOHR FIELD INFRASTRUCTURE (~70 km away) — it does NOT run to Port Said or make landfall at all. From Zohr, gas is processed at Zohr's existing offshore facilities, then separately piped onward via Zohr's own pre-existing ~218 km trunk line to the Damietta LNG terminal for liquefaction (not Port Said/El Gamil). 'Port Said' only appears in sourcing as a distance reference for Zohr's location ('190 km north of Port Said'), never as an actual pipeline terminus. The sheet's 90.0 km length corroborates this: it's the right order of magnitude for the short Cronos-Zohr subsea tieback (~70-90 km depending on source), and far too short for any direct run to Port Said or Damietta (which would be 250-300+ km). Recommend the tracker's endpoint/name be corrected from 'Port Said' to 'Zohr field infrastructure' or similar (Baird's call — flagged here, not applied). Start coord basis: No official surveyed coordinate for Cronos was found in any public source (Eni/TotalEnergies press releases, Cyprus CHC licensed-blocks page, Wikidata all omit it). Triangulated approximation combining two independently reported distances: ~70 km from the Zohr field (en.protothema.gr) and ~160-185 km SW of Cyprus's coast (offshore-mag.com: 185 km; discoveryalert.com.au / drillingcontractor.org: 160 km; maritime-executive.com: '90 nm' ≈ 167 km), anchored on Zohr's coordinate (33°00'N, 32°30'E, Wikidata). End coord basis: Zohr field-center coordinate (33°00'N, 32°30'E) per Wikidata (Q20894861). column109: CB: route guessed from endpoints — Two independent official documents describe this exact corridor under the name '吉林-延吉天然气管道' (Jilin-Yanji Natural Gas Pipeline), matching GEM's zh_alt '吉林吉化-延吉天然气管道': (1) a 2013 EIA first-public-notice from CNPC's pipeline arm (中国石油管道公司管道工程第二项目经理部, via 中石油东北炼化工程有限公司) states the route '起点为吉林市龙潭区（长岭——长春——吉林天然气管道吉化末站），终至位于延吉市大兴屯南侧的末站...沿线依次经过吉林市、延边朝鲜族自治州2个地级区域...吉林市段...经过吉林市、蛟河市，总长约136.7km；延边朝鲜族自治州路由经过敦化市、安图县、龙井市、延吉市，总长约173.6km，全线总长约310.3km。共设置9个截断阀室和3个分输站' (starts at the Jihua terminal station of the Changling-Changchun-Jilin gas pipeline in Longtan District, Jilin City; ends at a terminal station south of Daxingtun, Yanji City; passes through Jilin City, Jiaohe City, Dunhua City, Antu County, Longjing City, Yanji City; total ~310.3km; 9 block-valve chambers, 3 distribution stations). (2) A 2019-04-29 formal project approval (核准批复, 项目代码2018-222401-45-02-003878) from the Jilin Provincial Development & Reform Commission to project owner 吉林省能源集团国际管道有限公司 confirms the same start/end and route: '项目起点为吉林市拟建的兴安盟-吉林煤制天然气管道吉林末站，主要沿珲乌高速向东南方向敷设，途径蛟河市、敦化市、安图县、龙井市，最终抵达拟建的延吉综合站' -- new trunk 305km (DN813, 10MPa) + 7km branch, 3 new stations (蛟河分输站 Jiaohe, 敦化综合站 Dunhua, 延吉综合站 Yanji), 11 valve chambers, total investment RMB 1.647 billion. The same approval document also references a related, larger 2017-approved sister project extending further east to '珲春市综合站' (吉林-珲春天然气管道工程, 428km total, via Tumen and Hunchun) -- i.e. this Jilin-Yanji line is functionally the first (western) segment of a longer Jilin-to-Hunchun corridor. | IMPORTANT DISCREPANCY TO FLAG: GEM's payload StartLocation for P7700 is 'Yushu', but every source found for the segment name given ('JCIC-Yanji' / zh_alt '吉林吉化-延吉天然气管道') places the true start at JIHUA/Longtan District, JILIN CITY -- not Yushu. 'JCIC' most plausibly reads as 'Jilin Chemical Industrial Company' (吉化 = 吉林化学工业公司/吉林石化), i.e. the Jihua petrochemical complex, which sits in Jilin City, ~100km northwest of Yushu. A separate, newer generation of Yanbian-serving pipelines DOES originate at Yushu (see P7699/P7705's sourcing, and a 2025 duckduckgo search hit describing a Hulin-Changchun-pipeline 'Yanji branch' [虎林—长春天然气管道延吉支线项目] starting at '虎林-长春天然气管道榆树分输清管站' [the Yushu distribution/pigging station of the Hulin-Changchun pipeline] and ending at '延吉末站' -- but that source, www.eiafans.com/thread-1440530-1-1.html, was unreachable in this pass [connection refused, no Wayback snapshot] so it is NOT used as a ref here). Two plausible readings: (a) GEM's StartLocation field is simply wrong/stale for this row and should read 'Jilin' not 'Yushu'; or (b) P7700 is meant to represent the NEWER Yushu-origin alignment and the zh_alt Chinese name is an inherited/legacy label that no longer matches the current routing. Given the zh_alt name is an exact, unambiguous match to the Jilin City-origin project documented in two strong primary sources, I have used that alignment for the coordinates above, but this should be reconciled against GEM's StartLocation field before a route candidate is finalized -- it may turn out P7700 and P7705 (Yushu-Hunchun) are describing overlapping/successor alignments of the same underlying corridor.

column109: CB: route guessed from endpoints — Per Zhejiang Development & Reform Commission's official 14th Five-Year Plan for Coal, Petroleum and Natural Gas Development (fzggw.zj.gov.cn, published 2021-07-07 — the same document already cited by a prior researcher for this pipeline), the route is explicitly described as running '乐清登陆站-温州末站，管径1219mm，设计压力10MPa，长度约46公里' (Yueqing Landing Station to Wenzhou [line-end] Station, diameter 1219mm, design pressure 10MPa, length ~46km) — the 46km figure matches GEM's LengthMergedKm=46.00 exactly, strong corroboration this is the correct project. column109: CB: route guessed from endpoints — Resolved via the same presidency.eg national-projects registry (dated July 2019) that separately covers P7574, corroborated by petro-news.com's project-list summary (same 42in/165km/3.335B-EGP figures). Confidence: moderate — solid on the project's existence, corridor, and total length, but the SPECIFIC 73km sub-segment's own start/end are inferred from the sheet's segment label rather than independently measured in the source. Abu Sultan is confirmed as a real, named gas-grid station (also the tie-in point for P7574's separate line), consistent with the hint that it sits on the Great Bitter Lake side near Ismailia. SHEET CONFLICT: The presidency.eg source describes the FULL corridor as a single 42in/165km project across Cairo, Ismailia, AND Port Said governorates, serving MULTIPLE purposes (national-grid reinforcement, NAC power-station feed, plus supply to south-Cairo areas and Upper Egypt consumers) — not a simple point-to-point Abu Sultan→NAC line. column20: The Alaska Natural Gas Development Authority filed a right-of-way lease application dated April 4, 2005 with the State of Alaska for a buried 24-inch steel gas pipeline of about 148 miles from Glennallen to just west of Palmer, with a stated capacity of 1,000 million standard cubic feet per day. The application is the concrete step. The sponsor is a State of Alaska public corporation. Search results from the Alaska Division of Oil and Gas show a native lands report supporting a conditional right-of-way lease application, and a Petroleum News piece from September 2006 discusses the spur line, but neither was read for the length. A later Alaska Division of Oil and Gas summary calls it 143 miles; the application itself says 148. No sign of construction, a start year, or activity after about 2008 was found, so the status shelved with type inferred is a presumption and no URL backs it. Status needs a check by a person. The applicant is not in the owner list; the entity lookup found no exact match and the style tool found no legal form. Route not found, so no route is proposed. Only one source states the values, so the tier is medium. Extra context pages that load: https://dog.dnr.alaska.gov/Documents/SPCS/ANGDA/FinalReports/MiscellaneousReports/NativeLandReport.pdf and https://www.petroleumnews.com/pntruncate/28843979.shtml. The start location was recorded from the application text, which says the line begins in Glennallen on Ahtna lands.

Not an existing row. Checked ANR rows: Wisconsin Reliability (P5547, 48 mi, operating, different project) and Heartland (P7793, Illinois to Wisconsin, 70 mi, proposed) are separate. Northwoods is a 92 mile, 36 inch loop along ANR's mainline in Iron County, Michigan and Florence, Marinette, Oconto and Shawano Counties, Wisconsin, plus one new 4,700 horsepower compressor station in Shawano County and two meter stations. Concrete step: ANR entered FERC pre-filing on March 12, 2026 (docket PF26-6); formal application planned October 2026, certificate October 2027, in service November 1, 2029. Source is the EIA pipeline projects table for August 2026 (sheet Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, Excel row 94, project Northwoods Project, status Pre-applied, 92 mi, 36 in, 390 MMcf/d, 2029, 390,000 Dth/d in the description).
